cards.title: Set GA4 event data retention to 14 months at property creation
cards.summary: Change GA4's default two-month event data retention to 14 months immediately after creating a property so Explorations can use a longer historical window.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new GA4 property for an ecommerce store, or auditing an existing property before doing seasonal/year-over-year merchandising and product performance analysis.
steps: Open GA Admin and navigate to Data Settings > Data Retention (this may be listed under Property settings depending on the current GA4 interface, so verify the exact menu path in your account).
Change the event data retention period from the default 2 months to 14 months.
Click Save. If you are on a premium (360) version, longer periods may be selectable.
Do this as soon as the property is created rather than later, because retention governs how far back Explorations and certain reports can look.
After this is set, plan analyses (e.g., last year's Q4 product mix) knowing 14 months is the standard ceiling.
caveats: Retention only controls how long event data remains queryable in tools like Explorations; standard reports may aggregate differently.
Changing the setting later does not retroactively recover data that was already dropped under the shorter window.

cards.title: Register all business domains for cross-domain tracking in GA4
cards.summary: List every domain your store uses in GA4 domain configuration so sessions spanning multiple properties are attributed correctly.
cards.use_when: When your ecommerce operation runs across multiple domains or subdomains (e.g., main store and a separate checkout or regional domain) and you need accurate session and conversion attribution.
steps: Go to Admin > Data Streams and select your website data stream.
Scroll to Configure tag settings and open Configure your domains.
Add each domain your business uses that is tracked by the same GA4 property (e.g., example.com and another-website.com).
Enter the root domain only; entering example.com automatically covers all of its subdomains, so subdomains do not need separate entries.
If five domains are tracked by one property, add all five, then Save.
Confirm the setting afterward by testing a journey that crosses domains and checking that it stays in one session.
caveats: This setting is specifically about cross-domain tracking; it does not by itself fix other attribution gaps.
Only relevant if you actually track multiple domains with the same property.

cards.title: Exclude internal (employee) traffic from GA4 reports
cards.summary: Define internal traffic rules by IP and activate the data filter so staff visits do not pollute ecommerce metrics.
cards.use_when: When employees work from an office or have static IPs and you are making decisions from conversion rate, session, or product-performance reports that staff browsing would distort.
steps: In Admin, go to the tag settings area and click Show more, then Define internal traffic.
Click Create and add a rule naming the traffic (e.g., 'office IP') and a condition such as IP address equals your office IP.
Add multiple conditions if needed, but ensure the relevant IP addresses are included.
Go to Data Collection > Data Filters and find the internal traffic filter, which starts in testing mode.
Activate the filter so employee traffic is excluded going forward.
Re-check after activation that sessions drop to expected levels.
caveats: Works only where IPs are static; remote or dynamic-IP staff will not be covered reliably.
Activation excludes traffic from that point forward; it does not clean historical data.

cards.title: Extend GA4 session timeout and engagement timer (source opinion)
cards.summary: The presenter recommends raising the default 30-minute session timeout and the engaged-session timer, accepting fewer but longer sessions in exchange for cleaner landing-page data.
cards.use_when: When reviewing landing-page and acquisition reports and seeing many 'not set' landing pages or sessions that break up a single shopping visit.
steps: Go to Data Streams, select your website data stream, then Configure tag settings and Show more.
Open Adjust session timeout. Default is 30 minutes; the presenter usually sets at least 4 hours and often the maximum of 7 hours and 55 minutes.
Open the engaged-session timer setting and raise it from the default; the presenter considers 10 seconds too short and sets at least 30 seconds or more.
Save your changes.
Be aware of the trade-off the source states: longer timeouts can merge multiple daily visits into one session, reducing total session count, while reducing 'not set' landing pages.
caveats: This is explicitly the presenter's personal recommendation, and he notes some people disagree.
Merged sessions can understate visit frequency, which affects frequency-based retention analysis.

cards.title: Enable Google Signals to populate demographics and interests
cards.summary: Turn on Google Signals in GA4 so age, gender, and interest dimensions stop being empty, weighing advertising-feature and privacy implications first.
cards.use_when: When you want demographic or interest data to segment ecommerce audiences (e.g., which age bands drive purchases) but your reports currently show no data for those dimensions.
steps: Go to the GA Admin panel, then Data Collection, then Google Signals data collection.
Toggle the setting on; demographics like age, gender, and interest will begin populating after activation.
Expect a delay — the source notes it can take weeks for data to appear.
Before enabling, consider that turning it on activates certain Google advertising features; if your company is strict about legal requirements, consult the legal team first.
caveats: Requires user consent/data-collection eligibility; data may remain sparse if consent rates are low.
Enabling it links GA data to Google advertising features, so privacy/legal review is advised.

cards.title: Configure five foundational GA4 settings in the correct order
cards.summary: A starting checklist for a new GA4 property: data retention, domain configuration, internal traffic exclusion, session timing, and Google Signals.
cards.use_when: When onboarding a new ecommerce GA4 property or auditing an existing one before trusting its conversion and product reports.
steps: Use the Admin panel — most settings live at property level, though some exist at account level.
1) Data retention: raise from 2 months to 14 months and save immediately.
2) Domains: if tracking multiple sites in one property, register all root domains under Configure your domains.
3) Internal traffic: define employee IPs and activate the data filter so staff traffic is excluded.
4) Session timing (presenter's recommendation): extend session timeout and the engaged-session timer.
5) Google Signals: enable it if you want demographic/interest data, subject to legal review.
Treat this as a minimum baseline to consider, not a complete implementation; the source notes it only scratches the surface of GA4 setup.
caveats: Some steps (session timeout, Google Signals) are source opinions or carry privacy trade-offs, not universal mandates.
Menu paths and defaults can change across GA4 versions; verify the current interface.
